Question B-004-002-006.

Why the correct answer is right: A single diode passes only one polarity of an applied AC waveform, producing pulsating direct current at the output side.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "No signal": There is output during the conducting half-cycles, so no signal is not generally correct.
- sourceIndex 2: "Steady direct current": A single diode alone does not make perfectly steady DC; filtering would be needed to smooth the pulses.
- sourceIndex 3: "Pulsating alternating current": The current pulses are one direction, so calling them alternating current misses the rectifier action.
